# Section A results: signal quality (aligned SNR) and paired heart-rate error

*Generated by `scripts/analysis/section_A.py`. All exploratory (MASTER_PLAN section 4): no pass or fail here.*

## Limits to read first

- A valid aligned SNR exists only for the **new 100** recordings (and 12 first-50 recordings from the bridge run). The saved `snr_db` of the first 50 is invalid and is not used.
- SNR is computed only when the digitiser gave an output, and only on lead II.
- In-distribution: the digitiser was trained on pages from the same generator family, so these numbers describe this setup, not real-world photos.
- Arm C check (2026-11-05): most SNR loss on real captures was local timing wobble of the traced signal (+5 to +7 dB when each 2 s window was shifted separately), not noise. SNR therefore mixes noise and timing distortion.
- Excluded as unreliable: 15192_lr, 21205_lr.

## 2. Does a low SNR go with a wrong heart rate? (new 100, images with output)

Spearman correlation between SNR and absolute heart-rate error (negative = lower SNR, larger error), with a recording-level bootstrap interval. AUC = chance that a wrong page has a lower SNR than a right page (0.5 = no information).

| subset | n | n_wrong5 | spearman_snr_vs_abs_error | boot95 | spearman_snr_vs_wrong5 | auc_low_snr_flags_wrong | auc_boot95 |

| all 13 versions | 1265 | 86 | -0.734 | -0.79 to -0.68 | -0.286 | 0.828 | 0.78 to 0.87 |
| resolution | 297 | 52 | -0.753 | -0.81 to -0.69 | -0.464 | 0.853 | 0.81 to 0.90 |

| brightness | 296 | 10 | -0.682 | -0.77 to -0.57 | -0.282 | 0.95 | 0.88 to 0.99 |
| gridcontrast | 297 | 8 | -0.49 | -0.65 to -0.30 | -0.245 | 0.937 | 0.81 to 1.00 |
